name: China Sourcing Risk Audit Agent
description: AI agent that audits China sourcing risks: detects fake factories, gold-supplier badge fraud, sample switching, payment hijacking, customs/HS misclassification, and freight cost traps. Produces actionable checklists and red-flag reports for importers placing $5k-$50k first orders.

skills.name: Supplier Verification Audit
skills.description: Verifies whether a Chinese supplier is a real factory or a trading company/middleman: registry check (business license scope, registered capital, abnormal list), gold-supplier badge authenticity, payment routing red flags (personal accounts, uncle's company), and verification steps importers can run in under 30 minutes.
examples: Check if this Alibaba supplier is a real factory: [supplier link]
The factory asked me to wire 30% deposit to a personal account - is this a red flag?
How do I verify a Chinese company before placing my first order?

skills.name: Customs & Landed Cost Audit
skills.description: Audits total landed cost traps: volumetric weight math (LxWxH/5000), LCL destination port charges (CFS/document fees), de minimis threshold changes, HS code misclassification risk (12% error rate, retroactive duties up to 18 months), and container break-even cubic meter calculations.
examples: I'm importing low-value bulky items - how do I know if shipping will kill my margin?
What are the hidden port charges in LCL shipping from China?
My supplier says HS code doesn't matter - is that true?

skills.name: Payment & Wire Fraud Check
skills.description: Detects payment hijacking schemes: requests to wire deposits to personal/uncle's company accounts, invoice-swap fraud, advance payment traps before contract terms are locked, and 3 red flags that precede 90% of China sourcing scams.
examples: Supplier wants 50% deposit upfront - what should I negotiate?
Salesperson asked me to pay his new company instead of the factory - legit?
What are the warning signs of a China sourcing wire fraud?

skills.name: Sample Switch Audit
skills.description: Detects sample-switching schemes where suppliers send high-grade samples then ship lower-grade production: contract clauses that prevent it, QC inspection timing, sealed-sample comparison, and video verification tactics.
examples: How do I make sure my production matches the sample?
What contract clause prevents the factory from switching materials?
What QC checks should I run before the container ships?
